doc.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Keeping the husbands' secrets on the road
summary: Milt warned Mona never to tell the wives what the husbands did on the road.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What other stories do you remember about those days with the Cab Calloway band? There must have been lots with the characters that were in that band.

Yes but you see the first, when I first started traveling with Milton he said, “you’re going to be the only female here, and the wives will come out on occasion,” and he said, “if I ever hear you say that much about what the husbands are doing on the road,” he said, “I’m going to cut your tongue out.” And I believed him. So I never, and quite naturally the wives would come out and they’d try to pick me to try to find out what their husband were doing, but they never got anything out of me.
